Hi Liam / Emily —

Thanks for the clear list — below is a concise commercial summary and implementation notes you can include in the packet. I'll also drop a short commercial summary PDF to make it easier for finance/legal.

1) Options (high level)
- Monthly (pay-as-you-go): billed monthly based on actual usage against the pool; no prepay discount. Good if you expect bursty or unpredictable workloads.
- Annual prepay (reserved commit): customer prepays for a committed monthly throughput (e.g., X GPU-hours or reserved vGPU capacity) for 12 or 24 months in exchange for a discount. Discounts increase with commit size and term.

2) Discounting (typical bands) — illustrative only, final hinges on commit size:
- 12-month commit: ~12–20% off list depending on GPU SKU and committed units
- 24-month commit: ~18–27% off list at higher commit tiers
- Volume tiers: bigger pools (>= 32 A100-equivalent GPUs) trigger deeper pricing steps

3) True-up mechanics
- Quarterly reconciliation: we compare billed committed capacity vs actual consumption. If actual > committed, the overage is invoiced at the agreed overage rate for the quarter (capped to the next tier).
- End-of-term true-up: if sustained usage has grown, we propose a recommended new commit and amortize any prepaid delta across remaining months or issue a single adjustment invoice.
- Short-term bursts are handled via burst capacity (pay-as-you-go) to avoid hitting hard limits.

4) Billing / PO flow
- Standard flow: Redwood issues an initial invoice for the first prepay installment (if prepay), then monthly/quarterly invoices for usage reconciliation and any overage.
- PO upfront: accepted — we can reference PO numbers on invoices.
- Net terms: default is Net-30. We can consider Net-45/Net-60 for larger enterprise contracts with an approved credit check and signed SOW.

5) Guarantees & credits
- Throughput SLO: we commit to a baseline throughput and latency band for pinned pools. SLA credits are applied as a % credit on the next invoice per the SLO table in our terms. Credits are automatic once the outage is verified.

Next steps

Quick invoice flow notes from ops side —

- Invoice cadence: for annual prepay we issue an initial invoice for the prepaid amount (single or split per contract) and then monthly reconciliation invoices that reflect usage vs prepaid allocation.
- PO handling: please include PO number on all invoice PDFs and in the invoice metadata; we can accept PO-based payments routed to our AR team (ar@redwood.ai).
- True-up timing: we prefer quarterly true-ups (aligned with fiscal quarter) to minimize frequent adjustments; short bursts are charged as overage on the following invoice.
- Tax / cross-border: if Snowdrop will bill to a US entity, standard US tax/no VAT. If billing EU entity, please flag and we'll generate invoices with required VAT IDs.
- Payment methods: ACH or wire; we also accept card for initial prepay under $100k.

I'll prepare a sample amortization table for the commercial summary Rafael mentioned and upload it to the shared Drive link.

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity invoicing & prepay options — commercial summary attached

Liam —

Appended a short commercial summary (see attached) and a sample amortization schedule for the two examples you asked for. Quick highlights:

- $360k annual prepay (12-month): effectively ~ $30k/month recognized for the prepaid portion; we show a 14% discount vs list in the sample.
- $720k annual prepay (12-month, larger tier): sample shows ~18% discount and a lower effective $/GPU-hour.
- Overage rate: default is a negotiated overage rate at list * 0.95 for committed customers; this can be capped to the next tier to give predictability.
- SLA credits: verification is automated via our monitoring system; once an incident meets the SLA criteria we raise a credit which flows as an invoice-line credit on the next monthly reconciliation invoice. We track incidents in the Console and reference incident IDs on the credit memo.
- Net-45: for commits >= $500k we can offer Net-45 subject to a quick credit application (AR team). Alternatively, customers can provide an initial deposit equal to 25% of the commit and Net-30 on the remainder.

I've added HubSpot deal link and DocuSign powerform to accelerate signatures. If we have agreement on Net-45 or deposit route, Marissa will generate the invoice/PO instructions and I can route the SOW for signature.

Best,
Rafael
